title: Kafka Consumer Lag Injection — order-events topic
description: Suspends order-service consumers to simulate lag buildup. Validates that Prometheus alert KafkaConsumerLagHigh fires within 2 minutes and Alertmanager routes to PagerDuty.

steady-state-hypothesis.title: Kafka consumer lag is within normal bounds

arguments: LAG=$(curl -sf '${prometheus_url}/api/v1/query?query=kafka_consumer_group_lag{group="${consumer_group}"}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; data=json.load(sys.stdin); vals=[float(r['value'][1]) for r in data['data']['result']]; print(max(vals) if vals else 0)"); [ $(echo "$LAG < 100" | bc) -eq 1 ]
docker compose -f demand-forecast-platform/docker-compose.yml pause order-service && echo '[CHAOS] order-service paused — Kafka messages will accumulate on order.events'

for i in $(seq 1 2000); do echo "{\"orderId\":\"chaos-$i\",\"status\":\"PENDING\"}" | docker exec -i $(docker ps -qf name=kafka) kafka-console-producer --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --topic order.events; done && echo '[CHAOS] 2000 messages produced to order.events'

ALERT=$(curl -sf 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/alerts' | python3 -c "import sys,json; data=json.load(sys.stdin); alerts=[a for a in data['data']['alerts'] if a['labels'].get('alertname')=='KafkaConsumerLagHigh']; print(len(alerts))"); [ "$ALERT" -gt 0 ] && echo '[CHAOS] KafkaConsumerLagHigh alert confirmed firing'
docker compose -f demand-forecast-platform/docker-compose.yml unpause order-service && echo '[CHAOS] order-service resumed — draining lag'
